rootCause.repair: An independent private-Worker v2 lane now qualifies the actual forward payload and paired forward-compatible rollback, then deploys only that downloaded immutable artifact without rebuilding.
rootCause.bootstrapDeadlock: The retained private Worker predates the runtime guard, but predeployment smoke required the guard response marker before the guarded successor could be installed.
rootCause.bootstrapRepair: The exact retained guardless version may omit only the predeployment guard marker while still requiring the service principal and fixed GET/HEAD request contract. Postdeployment smoke always requires the exact guard marker. Runtime guard settings are injected through an exclusive owner-only temporary config, and binding transition verification permits only the governed additive settings while preserving every preexisting binding.
rootCause.rejectedStaleCause: The temporary-directory alias hypothesis did not explain run 30191466442. The trusted default temporary base had already been canonicalized and the run advanced through the real Wrangler dry run.
rootCause.runnerWorkspaceCause: Wrangler 4.110.0 dry-run created project-local .wrangler scratch beneath the guarded forward runtime directory. The required post-dry-run byte and tree revalidation then rejected that unapproved entry before the forward deployment Wrangler process could spawn.
rootCause.trustedTempAliasRepair: The default node:os.tmpdir() alias is canonicalized while caller-supplied aliases remain rejected. Owner-only 0700/0600 modes, no-symlink checks, cleanup, and secret-output prohibitions remain unchanged.
rootCause.wranglerScratchIsolationRepair: Every dry-run, deployment, and rollback invocation receives one fixed, phase-specific --outdir inside an owner-only 0700 scratch directory that is a sibling of the guarded forward and rollback roots. The three outdirs are distinct, non-user-controlled, symlink-rejected, cleaned with the runtime workspace, and never allow .wrangler inside either guarded payload root.
rootCause.node24CleanupCause: The clean Node 24.4.1 runner correctly rejected the substituted symlink, then the test fixture used rmSync on that directory symlink and Node 24 returned ERR_FS_EISDIR during cleanup. The same cleanup happened to succeed under Node 25, so the local current-Node matrix did not expose the portability defect.
rootCause.node24CleanupRepair: The Infrastructure-owned fixture now removes the known symlink with unlinkSync before recreating the directory. The security assertion, symlink rejection, real Wrangler dry run, and production boundaries are unchanged.
rootCause.canonicalSmokeCause: The authenticated service principal passed Cloudflare Access, but the fixed smoke plan requested /index.html. Cloudflare Workers static assets use auto-trailing-slash HTML handling and return a 307 canonicalization redirect from /index.html to /. Universal redirect denial correctly stopped every run before deployment.
rootCause.canonicalSmokeRepair: The fixed GET/HEAD plan now requests only the canonical root HTML path. The noncanonical /index.html alias is omitted from the client plan, every redirect remains fail-closed, and a Miniflare integration test proves the repository assets return 200 for / and 307 to / for /index.html.
rootCause.sharedPublicRollbackDriftCause: Removing /index.html from the shared runtime guard changed the generated public Worker bundle even though the corrective targets only the private Worker.
rootCause.sharedPublicRollbackPreservationRepair: Infrastructure restored the historical read-only guard alias byte-for-byte, isolated canonical-path filtering inside the non-Worker smoke client, and restored the private forward-payload continuity pin.
rootCause.propagationFailureCause: The first immediate postdeployment root request was Access-authorized and returned 2xx before the newly active Worker guard had propagated to that edge, so the exact guard marker was absent.
rootCause.propagationRepair: Postdeployment readiness now requires both the exact guard marker and the exact Cloudflare Worker version ID supplied through the CF_VERSION_METADATA binding. The same version is required on every full-smoke response, including when an older Worker serves byte-identical HTML. Fetch, response inspection, and body cancellation share one bounded deadline; redirects, non-2xx, invalid markers or versions, transport failures, and deadlines fail closed into the one qualified forward rollback.
rootCause.rollbackRootGuardGap: The forward-compatible rollback originally routed only /api/* through the generated Worker wrapper, while the propagation probe requests the canonical root. A rollback root could therefore bypass both the authenticated guard marker and CF_VERSION_METADATA proof.
rootCause.rollbackRootGuardRepair: The rollback routes only canonical / and the existing /api/* namespace through the generated wrapper. A composed test proves an authenticated rollback root response contains both the exact guard marker and the exact Worker version while ordinary static assets and approved Dashboard behavior remain unchanged.
rootCause.guardConvergenceGap: The postdeployment readiness fence proved only the canonical root while the fixed acceptance plan also checks static assets. Forward and rollback used different assets.run_worker_first representations, so a root response could carry the exact guard marker and Worker version before every fixed static path crossed the same Worker boundary.
rootCause.guardConvergenceRepair: Forward and rollback initially used the same selective ["/*"] route-pattern boundary. Each propagation attempt evaluated the entire fixed GET/HEAD plan, accepted only when every probe carried the exact guard marker and exact Worker version, emitted only fixed nonsecret probe classifications, and never retries unsafe response classes.
rootCause.forwardPayloadPinCorrection: The first owner commit carried a payload digest derived from a symlinked dependency tree. Infrastructure independently regenerated the payload with a materialized dependency tree matching the clean GitHub runner, pinned the exact digest, and preserved all runtime behavior.
rootCause.unconditionalGuardRoutingGap: The selective route-pattern array ["/*"] did not provide the unconditional Worker-first security invariant for the cached runtime-pools asset. The valid 2xx response bypassed the Worker guard and therefore lacked its exact marker.
rootCause.prematureConvergenceDeadlineGap: The smoke fence advertised a 46.5-second convergence window but exhausted twelve fast attempts after roughly 16.5 seconds because acceptance was controlled by attempt count rather than measured elapsed time.
rootCause.unconditionalGuardRoutingRepair: Forward and rollback now require Cloudflare's boolean true unconditional Worker-first mode and reject every route-pattern array. The full-plan smoke fence uses a monotonic 46.5-second deadline with no attempt-count acceptance limit; unsafe response classes still fail immediately into the one verified forward rollback.
rootCause.concurrentSmokeFailureCause: Postdeployment readiness launched the entire fixed 15-request GET/HEAD plan concurrently under individual 2.5-second deadlines. One transport stall rejected the batch, and plan-order classification reported ROOT_GET even though the canonical root remained directly reachable after rollback.
rootCause.smokeSequencingRepair: Postdeployment propagation readiness now uses only canonical GET / under the existing monotonic deadline. After the exact guard marker and Worker version converge, the complete fixed 15-request GET/HEAD smoke runs exactly once in deterministic sequence. Unsafe responses and transport failures remain immediate fail-closed rollback triggers, and no blanket retry was added.
rootCause.probePropagationFailureCause: Canonical readiness reached the new private Worker, but the immediately following fixed-plan root request reached an older edge instance. The sequential plan treated that bounded stale-version propagation state as final and entered the qualified rollback.
rootCause.probePropagationRepair: After canonical readiness, each fixed GET/HEAD probe may wait only through missing guard evidence or missing/stale Worker-version evidence under one shared monotonic 46.5-second deadline. Redirects, non-2xx responses, malformed markers or versions, transport failures, and nonadvancing clocks still fail immediately; accepted probes remain sequential and application writes remain zero.
rootCause.browserHealthDiagnosticGap: The browser acceptance runner collapsed eight viewport-specific health causes into one HEALTH result, preventing a safe corrective from distinguishing console, runtime, network, and external-request failures.
rootCause.browserHealthDiagnosticRepair: The runner now emits only one fixed viewport-and-cause classification while preserving fail-closed acceptance, zero retries, zero arbitrary diagnostic content, and zero secret or claim-value disclosure.
